Rocky Desert Works
Rocky Desert · one base round one lake, planned by phase from the first hour · game coordinates

Rocky Desert Works

Base round the Rocky Desert Lake. A camp between two pure iron nodes, a works of three halls across a 16 m street from it, a storage depot and a plaza for the HUB along that street, a power station on a terrace over the lake, steel and concrete on the plain behind it, the later halls straight across the water, and an oil yard on the coast. The last two phases get a second works on the plain to the west, with a pier over the sea. Every pad has room round it to become a building.

How the base is laid out

  • Main Street, 16 m wide and never built on. Its north half carries every belt on one rack; its south half stays clear to walk and drive, with the hypertube overhead later.
  • The Works, north of the street: Hall 1 for Reinforced Iron Plates and Smart Plating, Hall 2 for copper, Hall 3 for the plates and rods you build with, and the Space Elevator on its own pad.
  • The Camp, south of the street: the storage depot with one bay for each part, the HUB plaza and its terrace with every bench at its real size, the pure iron node Iron A, and the biofuel depot.
  • The Lake Bank, phase 2: the power station where you asked for it, as a terrace over the bank, with four Water Extractors in the lake off its corner.
  • The West Plain, south of the station: the Concrete works in phase 1 and the Steel Works in phase 2.
  • The North Shore, across the lake by a causeway: the phase 2 hall in two floors, the Rotor works and the Assembly hall, and beside them the Engine hall of phase 3.
  • The West Field, phase 3: the Control hall, on the big flat field behind the ridge west of the lake, 250 m from the Concrete works by its own rack.
  • The Oil Coast, phase 3: an oil yard beside a pure oil node and a fuel power yard beside a normal one, 1240 m to the south-west, on their own map.
  • The West Plain and the West Pier, phases 4 and 5: a second works on the flat ground beyond the West Field, with its own street, and a deck over the sea for the largest machines.
  • First foundation: north-west corner at -1688, -320. It is the south-east foundation of Hall 1.

Everything on the drawings can be clicked for its position and what to do with it. The site plan can be dragged, zoomed and switched by phase. Every Splitter and Merger carries an arrow showing which way the flow runs through it. How each block is built is in the Builder's Handbook.

What you asked for, and what I did

  • Power station at -1960, -360: moved there. It is the bank down to the lake, not flat ground: 54 of its 90 squares are clear on the map, 30 have a contour line and 6 a rock edge, and map heights inside it fall from -6.5 to -14.3 m. So it is drawn as a terrace level with Main Street, on pillars toward the lake. Walk it before you lay it.
  • A bigger HUB plaza: 6 by 3 with a 4 by 1 terrace. The HUB, the AWESOME Sink, the Craft Bench, the Equipment Workshop, the MAM and the AWESOME Shop are each drawn at the size the wiki gives, with at least 3 m to walk between any two.
  • Storage, and you were right twice: a container's belt ports are at its two ends, so the bays stand end-on to the street; and a bay needs no Splitter. One belt runs straight into one container. Drawing 3 shows it.
  • Every hall is drawn machine by machine: phase 2 in drawings 10 and 11, phase 3 in drawings 12 and 13, the fuel power yard in drawing 17. Only the North Shore reserve is still an empty floor with a card.
  • More room: Main Street is 16 m wide and halls stand 16 m apart. Two gaps are 8 m: between Hall 2 and the Elevator pad, and beside the Concrete works. The ground gives no more there.
  • Steel, concrete and oil: the Steel Works and the oil yard from the Grass Fields plans are here, redrawn, with a new Concrete works at the limestone node.
  • Hypertubes: a line and four entrances are marked, so nothing gets built in their way.

And one to know

  • Copper is behind a ridge about 35 m high, east of the Works. Its belt has to climb it on Conveyor Lifts or go round its north end. Walk it before you lay the belt.
Drawing 3 · Main Street close up, north up, real sizes, grid lines every 20 m

The HUB plaza and the storage depot

Click a belt, a container or a building.

How a part finds its bay without a Splitter

  • The rack is not one belt. It is a stack of separate belts, three wide and three high (four from Tier 3), and each belt carries one part only. The Iron Plate belt starts at Hall 3's plate Constructor and ends in the Iron Plate container. Nothing else is ever on it.
  • So nothing has to be sorted. A Splitter is for one belt that feeds several places. Each storage belt feeds one place, so it simply turns off the rack opposite its bay and runs into the container.
  • If it were one mixed belt, you would be right: every bay would need a Smart Splitter to pick its part out. That works too, but Smart Splitters are MAM research and one mixed belt jams when any single bay is full.

The rack, looking west

Click a slot. Each slot is one belt on Stackable Conveyor Poles (Tier 2, Logistics Mk.2). Before that, lay the first belts side by side on the ground along the same line.

  • One belt keeps one slot the whole way, so you can always follow it by eye.
  • South column leaves first. On each level the south belt turns off at the easternmost bay, then the middle one, then the north one. A belt turning south therefore never meets another at its own height.
  • The bottom level is for ore and coal, which pass the depot without stopping.
  • The top level comes later: a second coal belt at Tier 3, then the belts that carry finished parts east to the Space Elevator.

A storage bay

  • A container's belt ports are at its two ends. So it stands end-on to the street: belt in at the north end, out at the south end.
  • One bay, one belt, one container. When the container is full the belt backs up and the hall behind it rests. Nothing is lost.
  • Getting parts out. Walk the south side and open any container: you take from it by hand, from any side. Hook a belt to the south end only when a part has to travel on.
  • Growing. Containers stack: in phase 2 a second one goes on each bay for a second part. From Tier 4 an Industrial Storage Container is the same 5 by 11 m with twice the room.

Phase 2: the only Splitters at the depot

In phase 2 four storage belts also feed the Assembly hall. Where each turns off the rack for its bay, put a Splitter: one outlet into the bay as before, the other on along the rack, up the service lane and over the causeway. The Assembly hall takes what it needs and its belt fills; everything else then goes into the bay.

Phase 3 adds none here. The Control hall's share is split off further on, where each of those belts turns into the service lane: the schedule above says where.

What the Space Elevator asks for

Progress is the Space Elevator. Each phase you deliver unlocks the next two tiers, so these numbers are the real length of the game. The times are how long the factory on this plan must run to make each part; build faster than that and you wait, build twice the line and you halve it.

Phase 1 · unlocks Tiers 3 and 4
PartAskedMade where, and from whatRateRunning time
Smart Plating50Hall 1, Assembler SP: 1 Reinforced Iron Plate and 1 Rotor each. Rotors by hand at the Craft Bench2 a minute25 min

Smart Plating cannot be crafted by hand, so the Assembler in Hall 1's corner is not optional. Rotors can: 50 of them are 250 Iron Rods and 1,250 Screws at the Craft Bench, and the Screws are another 313 rods, so about 19 minutes of Hall 3's rods in all. The Space Elevator itself costs 500 Concrete, 250 Iron Plates, 400 Iron Rods and 1,500 Wire: 25 minutes each of the Concrete works and of Hall 2's Wire.

Versatile Framework1,000Assembly hall, drawing 11: 1.875 Modular Frames and 22.5 Steel Beams a minute, the whole of the Steel Works' beams3.75 a minute4 h 27 min
Automated Wiring100Assembly hall, drawing 11: 1.5 Stators and 30 Cable a minute, the whole of Hall 2's Cable. Tier 41.5 a minute1 h 07 min

Versatile Framework is a Tier 3 recipe; the Stator and Automated Wiring are Tier 4. Hall 1 makes 5 Reinforced Iron Plates a minute, and phase 2 uses exactly 5: 2 for Smart Plating and 3 for Modular Frames. Smart Plating sets the pace: 8 h 20 min of running. To go faster, build a twin of Hall 1 as soon as phase 1 is in: 4 Smart Plating a minute, and the Rotor block already makes the 4 Rotors.

Rotors set the pace: 12 h 30 min of running. The Rotor works makes 4 a minute, and every Modular Engine takes 6: four in its two Motors and two in its two Smart Plating, which the Engine hall makes itself. Everything else is sized to finish in the same time: the Control hall makes its 100 units in step, and the Steel Works' beams are split between Versatile Framework and Heavy Modular Frames.

A head start for nothing. Those times are from a standing start, and phase 3 never has one. Leave every phase 2 line running after its own quota is in, and finished parts pile up in containers. As drawn, by the time phase 2's Smart Plating is delivered there are about 875 Versatile Framework in the container on the Elevator pad and 1,000 Rotors in bay 3. With those in hand phase 3 takes about 9 h 54 min, set by Reinforced Iron Plates. Carry the Rotors north and drop them into a Storage Container set in the Engine hall's rotor belt; the Versatile Framework is already where it has to be.

Going faster still in phase 3 takes three things at once, because the three parts share the same plates, Rotors and beams: a twin of Hall 1, a second Rotor works, and half as much steel again. Together they bring phase 3 down to 8 h 20 min; any one of them alone does nothing. The oil yard has room to spare either way: phase 3 takes 7,500 Rubber and 8,400 Plastic, and the yard makes that in three and a half hours.

Phase 4 is sized to take 16 h 40 min of running. That is the time for the Elevator's parts and for the parts the Tier 7 and Tier 8 milestones cost, which the same lines make first. Modular Engines and Versatile Framework are the two parts home still makes: the Engine hall's 0.67 a minute is just enough for the 625 engines the rockets take, and the Assembly hall makes the 1,250 Versatile Framework three times over. Everything else comes from the West Plain. Nuclear Pasta looks small at 100, but each one is 200 Copper Powder, which is 1,200 Copper Ingots.

Phase 5 is sized to take 33 h 20 min of running, and copper sets it. 1,100 Nuclear Pasta, a hundred of them inside the Singularity Cells, are 1.32 million Copper Ingots: 893 copper ore a minute for all of that time, with Miners Mk.3 on all three copper nodes of the plain and on the node at home. Nothing else on the list comes near it. More copper is the only thing that shortens phase 5: Power Shards in those four Miners, or an alternate recipe from a hard drive that makes more ingots from the ore.

Added up: 71 h 15 min of running for the five phases as drawn, with every line built and fed. Building them comes on top. Phases 4 and 5 are sized longer than the first three on purpose: a works that made them in half the time would be twice the floor, twice the ore and twice the power.

Start with eight

One pure coal node with a Miner Mk.1 gives 120 coal a minute, which a Mk.2 belt carries. That feeds exactly eight generators, and eight generators drink exactly three extractors. So build the four western pairs and E1 to E3 first: 600 MW.

Add G5, G10 and E4 when Logistics Mk.3 lets one belt carry more and the Miner Mk.2 lets the node give it.

A terrace, not a floor on the ground

The ground under it falls about 8 m from south to north. Lay the first row of foundations along its south edge, level with Main Street, and build north from there; the floor carries on level over the bank. Pillars under the north half are for looks: foundations do not need them.

Water goes uphill

The terrace stands well above the lake and a Water Extractor lifts water only 10 m by itself. One Pipeline Pump Mk.1 on each of the two pipes, at the shore, adds 20 m. Pumps are unlocked with Coal Power, the same milestone as the generators.

Two pipes, not one: a Mk.1 pipe carries 300 m³ a minute and four extractors give 480. Both run straight south from the extractors down the lane east of the station and turn into the aisle; the longer is about 140 m.

Power home

Power Towers are Tier 4. At Tier 3, run a row of Power Poles along the north edge of Main Street, about every 40 m. At Tier 4 the two towers on the plan replace it with one line of 174 m.

Drawing 15 · The oil coast, north up, 1 small square = 1 foundation (8 m), numbers are heights in metres

The oil coast

Phase 3 needs Plastic and Rubber, and both come from crude oil. The nearest is on the south-west coast, 1240 m from Hall 1: four nodes round a flat beach about a metre above the sea. As in the Oil Lake plan, the yard is built at the oil and joined to home by a power line.

Why coke and a Sink

Plastic and Rubber both leave Heavy Oil Residue behind. If it has nowhere to go, the Refineries stop. Two more Refineries turn it into Petroleum Coke and an AWESOME Sink eats the coke, so nothing can back up, and the Sink pays coupons.

Why two oil nodes

One node feeds the parts and the other feeds the power, on separate pipes. A generator burns less when the grid needs less, so its fuel line backs up; if the Plastic and Rubber shared that line they would stop too.

Drawing 18 · Phases 4 and 5 · the whole base, north up, grid lines every 500 m

Phases 4 and 5: the West Plain

The last two phases take ten times what phase 3 did, and three things home does not have: bauxite, quartz and nitrogen, then SAM. They also take more copper and iron than the three nodes by the lake can give. So they get a works of their own, 790 m west of the lake, on a plain with six iron and three copper nodes on it and the sea beside it. Home keeps running as it is and sends two parts west: Modular Engines and Versatile Framework.

Click a line or a mark. Dashed lines are directions over ground nobody has walked: the lengths are as drawn.

How it is laid out

  • West Street, 16 m wide, runs from the West Field to the shore. Like Main Street it is never built on and carries one rack; every belt between two halls is one belt on it.
  • Five halls on the plain, each with its dock on the street: copper, iron and steel, frames, electronics and aluminium.
  • The West Pier: a deck over the sea at the street's west end, for the machines that are too big for the plain. The Propulsion hall in phase 4, the Quantum hall in phase 5.
  • The oil coast grows: a Plastic yard, a second fuel power yard on a deck over the bay, and the oil well.
  • Two railways, each one track with one train: the Coast Line brings Plastic and Rubber over a viaduct across the bay, the North Line quartz and SAM. Caterium and bauxite come by belt, nitrogen by pipe, coal on the rack from home.
  • Every hall is the same idea: a bus of belts down one side, one belt for each part, and rows of machines fed from it. Learn one and you can read them all.

How to read a hall of phases 4 and 5

  • The bus is the bundle of lines down one side. Each line is one belt or pipe carrying one part, and has a number at the dock end. The table beside the drawing says what each is.
  • A row is one part. Its feed lines leave the bus and run along the top of the row; a hollow square is a Splitter, one in front of each machine but the last. One collector runs back along the bottom; a filled square is a Merger.
  • Rows side by side share a band. The row nearest the bus has its lines nearest the machines, so no line crosses another on the floor.
  • Crossing the bus: a feed leaves its own bus line and crosses the others one step up, on Stackable Conveyor Poles. In the game, stack the bus lines; they are drawn side by side so you can tell them apart.
  • Nothing to set on most machines: each stays at 100% and rests when its belt runs short. The card says what share of the time it runs.
  • The big ones are clocked down: a Particle Accelerator, a Converter and a Quantum Encoder draw hundreds of megawatts, so each card gives a clock speed that makes just what the phase asks.
  • Blue lines are pipes; a ring is a Pipeline Junction.
  • Power: one line of Power Poles along each row, as in the handbook. From Tier 4 a Power Pole Mk.2 holds seven lines and from Tier 6 a Mk.3 holds ten: the wiki has the tiers, I have not re-read them.

The oil coast grows

Phase 4 takes 231 Plastic a minute, six times what the oil yard makes, and the power the new halls draw has to come from somewhere. Room for what comes later

Hypertubes, Tier 4

  • The line is on the site plan in purple: overhead along the south edge of Main Street, up the service lane, round the station's corner and along the causeway to the North Shore.
  • Four entrances are marked: beside the plaza terrace, at the Works, at the service lane and on the North Shore.
  • Until Tier 4, build nothing on that line. That is all it asks.

The service lane

  • 16 m of bare ground east of the power station and the Steel Works, at x = -1868. Everything that goes to or from the west runs down it: two water pipes, coal, iron ore, steel, concrete.
  • Each has its own line in the lane, 3 m apart, so they never cross on the ground. Where one must cross another, raise it one step on Stackable Conveyor Poles.

Belts faster than Mk.1

  • Every hall is drawn for Mk.1 and Mk.2 belts. When Mk.3 arrives, the same floors take twice the machines: the gaps between rows are there for that.

More to build, when you want to

None of these is needed. Each has a place kept for it.

WhatWhenWhere and how
Walls and roofs on the hallsAny tier; pieces from the AWESOME ShopEvery pad has at least 8 m of lane round it, 16 m between halls, so a wall on the floor's edge never meets another building. Handbook, last section.
A lookout over the lakeTier 1, Base BuildingA Lookout Tower on the north edge of Main Street, west of Hall 1, sees the whole lake and the power terrace.
A twin of Hall 1Tier 2Smart Plating sets the pace of phase 2 at 2 a minute. A second Reinforced Iron Plate line with its own Smart Plating Assembler doubles it: the Rotor block already makes 4 Rotors a minute.
Rotors by beltTier 2, Part AssemblyHandbook module 9. Phase 1 gets by on 50 hand-made Rotors; the 1,000 Smart Plating of phase 2 need this block, so it is the first thing in the phase 2 hall.
Overflow to the SinkMAM, Caterium researchPut a Smart Splitter in a bay's belt just before its container: the middle outlet into the container, one side outlet set to Overflow and run to the AWESOME Sink. The hall never stops and the spare parts pay coupons.
Hard drivesMAM, from Tier 1Crash sites hold hard drives. Each one researched in the MAM offers alternate recipes; the ones that save Screws and Iron Rods are worth taking first.
Power ShardsMAM, Power SlugsSlugs become Power Shards, and a shard overclocks a machine. The first ones belong in Hall 1's Smart Plating Assembler and the Rotor works: they set the pace of phase 2.
A tractor or truck runTier 3, Vehicular TransportMain Street's south half is kept clear for it. A Truck Station at the service lane, and later a route to the oil coast along the tower line.
Power StorageTier 4, Expanded Power InfrastructureA row of batteries on the station terrace's west end rides out a coal hiccup.
The Blueprint DesignerTier 4, FICSIT Blueprints32 by 32 m. The North Shore reserve, north of the Engine hall, is kept for it.
Hypertube to the oil coastTier 4, HypertubesFollow the power towers, 1.3 km. It also makes carrying Rubber and Plastic home a short trip.
A faster phase 3Tiers 5 and 6A twin of Hall 1, a second Rotor works and half as much steel again, all three together, cut phase 3 from 12 h 30 min to 8 h 20 min.
A second oil yardTier 5The pure node in the south of the oil coast is spare, with flat ground round it.
A train before phase 4Tier 6, Monorail Train TechnologyThe Coast Line of phase 4 can be built as soon as trains are unlocked, and from the first day it carries the Rubber and Plastic of phase 3.
DronesTier 8, Aeronautical EngineeringA Drone Port at an outpost and one on West Street carry nine stacks a trip over any ground. Worth it if the North Line's ground turns out badly; they need fuel, and I have not worked out how much.

If something stops

What you seeWhy, and what to do
Everything is darkThe grid asked for more than the generators make, and the fuse tripped. Switch something off, then pull the fuse lever in any generator.
The power station will not restartCoal generators need water, and the Water Extractors need power. Keep the biofuel depot wired to the grid with fuel in it: it starts the extractors, and the station follows.
A machine stands idleIt is waiting: either its inlet is empty or its outlet is full. Follow the belt back to the first machine that is not idle; the fault is just before it.
A belt is full and stillIts container is full. That is the plan working: the hall behind it rests until you take parts out.
The burners are outNo fuel. Biomass Burners only burn while something draws power, so a full container lasts longer than it looks.
A Miner is not runningEvery Miner needs a power line. Plant Power Poles along its belt.

Pace and blueprints

What sets the length of the game is the parts each milestone and each Space Elevator phase asks for. No mod in the pack changes those. These are the mods that can shorten the road to them, and what to do about each.

ModWhat it speeds upRisk to the paceWhat to do
Faster Manual CraftingHand crafting speeds up with every item, to 25 times normal by defaultHigh in the first hoursCapped at 4 times, building up at 0.1 a step. Set on Scott's PC on 13 Nov 2026; the server and every other PC need the same file. Hand crafting stays a chore worth automating
Industrial EvolutionUpgraded machines with a production multiplier, researched in the MAM. A bigger multiplier costs more to buildHigh from the mid gameLeave its MAM tree alone until phase 2 is delivered, and never use its /ie UnlockAll command
Megaprojects: Water DamFree power, 250 MW from each unfinished damLow for usNone of its three sites is near the Rocky Desert
Refined PowerWind, water and solar power that burns nothingMediumBuild the coal station first. Treat wind and solar as a phase 3 reward
Progressive BlueprintersSmall blueprint designers before Tier 4LowThey are 1 to 3 foundations across: decorations and small repeats, not factories
Smart!, Infinite Zoop, Move Tool, Curve BuilderFaster building. Everything placed costs the normal partsNone on progressKeep. Infinite Zoop's Cheater Mode stays off, as it is now
LithiumCheaper alternate recipes from Tier 7LowIts extra Space Elevator parts are off by default; leave them off or turn them on for a longer end game

The short version

  • Two things do most of the work: the hand-crafting cap, and holding Industrial Evolution back until phase 2 is delivered. The capped settings file is in the repository under packs/configs; it must be the same on the server and on every PC.
  • Create the world with the game's normal settings. Advanced Game Settings stay off on the server.
  • Nothing here is measured. I have read each mod's own page and its settings file, not timed a playthrough.

Can we use blueprints from the start?

  • Not the downloaded ones. The base game unlocks the Blueprint Designer at Tier 4. The repository holds 194 blueprints; the 15 picked for the early game still need Mk.2 belts or better, all but one.
  • The ImKibitz packs are for later. 179 blueprints made in the Tier 6 and Tier 9 designers. 87 have no belts in them: roads, platforms, walls, walkways and pipe runs. Most of the rest use Mk.5 or Mk.6 belts.
  • Small ones, early. The pack's Progressive Blueprinters adds designers 1, 2 and 3 foundations across. The first asks you to gather a full stack of every basic material.
  • The handbook is the early blueprint. Its eleven modules are drawn to be built by hand from the first hour, anywhere.

What I checked, and what I did not

Checked

  • Every floor square against the Satisfactory Calculator map at its deepest zoom, 4.4 pixels to the metre, in three surveys: home, the oil coast, and the ground between. The page will not build if a floor other than the power station touches a square with a contour, a rock edge or water in it, if two floors are closer than 8 m, if a floor stands in Main Street or the service lane, or if an extractor is not wholly over deep water.
  • The map's position formula, against a pond whose place was confirmed in the game in the Grass Fields.
  • Node positions and heights against the map's data file. 10 map heights on and beside the flat home floors read -7.7 to -5 m.
  • The 22 Lithium nodes the mod adds, read from the mod's own source: none is under a floor. The nearest is 230 m from Hall 1.
  • Every Power Tower stands on clear ground, and no span is over 264 m on the map.
  • Each hall's line fits its floor exactly, no machine or pole overlaps another, the recipe arithmetic holds, and every Splitter and Merger sits on a belt.
  • On the wiki, on 13 Nov 2026: what each Space Elevator phase asks for and unlocks; what every HUB upgrade and every Tier 1 and Tier 2 milestone unlocks; the tiers of Power Towers, Hypertubes, the Miner Mk.2, the belt marks, Oil Processing and Petroleum Power; that Smart Plating cannot be hand-crafted and a Rotor can; the recipes and tiers of the Modular Frame, Versatile Framework, Stator, Automated Wiring, Motor, Modular Engine, Circuit Board, Computer, Encased Industrial Beam, Heavy Modular Frame and Adaptive Control Unit; the Manufacturer's size and power; and the sizes of the HUB, the Space Elevator, the Storage Container, the Craft Bench, the Equipment Workshop, the MAM, the AWESOME Sink and the AWESOME Shop; that a Storage Container has 24 slots and the Space Elevator six belt inlets; and the stack sizes used for carrying and storing: 200 for Rubber and Plastic, 100 for Rotors, 50 for Versatile Framework, Automated Wiring and Adaptive Control Units.
  • Where a Storage Container's belt ports are: read from real blueprints in the repository, where belts join a container 4 m from its centre along its length, at both ends.
  • Phases 4 and 5. Every recipe, what the two phases and the milestones of Tiers 7 to 9 ask for, and the size, power and belt and pipe ports of every machine, read from the wiki on 13 Nov 2026. The page will not build if a phase takes more ore, oil, gas or water than its Miners and Extractors give, if a hall on the plain touches a rock edge or water, if a hall on a deck touches anything but water, or if two halls are closer than 8 m.
  • The West Plain, surveyed like home: 1160 squares of hall with no rock edge on the map, and 21 map heights on and beside them between -5 and 1.8 m.
  • The page itself in a browser: zoom, drag, phases, cards, layers, legend and ticks.

Not checked in the game

  • Nobody has stood on this ground. The map is a drawing of the world, not the world. If rock taller than you stands inside a floor outline, stop and tell me the coordinates.
  • The power station's bank. The map says it falls about 8 m and has a rock edge along its north-west corner; I have reasoned that the edge is the lip of the drop, not rock that rises.
  • Where you land. The game drops you somewhere in the Rocky Desert start area; the walk to the lake is not measured.
  • That four Water Extractors place where drawn. Test them before laying the station floor.
  • The route of the coal belt down the plateau and across the ridge, and the copper belt's way over it.
  • The North Shore floors are clear on the map, with one map height beside the phase 2 hall and one beside the Engine hall: -3.2 and -3.2 m, so 3 to 5 m above the home plain.
  • Iron C's ore belt to the Rotor works, round the lake's north-east shore.
  • The causeway is a line on the map, not a design. 112 m of it is over the lake and no rock edge is on it.
  • The oil coast and the tower line. The beach reads -16.8 m at the one map height on it; heights along the line come from the nearest map marker, up to 120 m away.
  • Which way the HUB's door, the Sink's inlet and the benches face. Everything on the plaza has room on all sides for that reason.
  • The West Field and the way to it. The field is clear on the map, with two map heights of -3.3 and -1.7 m. The rack's line has no rock edge and no deep water on it, but it crosses the lake's outlet stream and passes a ridge 60 m high; its own heights are not known.
  • That the Space Elevator stops taking a part once it has what the phase asks for. The wiki does not say, and the Versatile Framework container on the Elevator pad relies on it. If the Elevator keeps taking them, unhook its belt once the 1,000 are in, so the container fills.
  • How Rubber and Plastic come home from the oil coast: carried, or on belts along the towers over ground that is not surveyed for a belt.
  • The map data is from game build 492064; the game is now at 517554. Patch 1.2.1.0 added a limestone node in the Rocky Desert that may not be in it.
  • Phases 4 and 5 are a plan from the map and the wiki, further from the game than anything above. No hall of the West Plain has been built, and the exact place of the belt and pipe ports on a Blender, a Particle Accelerator, a Converter or a Quantum Encoder is not drawn.
  • The Coast Line is checked square by square on the map: water or clear ground all the way, no rock edge. How deep the bay is, and whether anything stands in it, is not known.
  • The routes of the North Line, the caterium and bauxite belts and the nitrogen pipe. They are directions with the few map heights there are, and each crosses rock edges or a stream on the map. The quartz and SAM nodes are in a cave, and how their ore gets out of it is not known.
  • That a deck can be built where the pier and fuel power yard 2 are drawn. The squares are water on the map; the depth, and whether anything stands in it, are not known.
  • The rock edges the map shows in West Street at x = -2696, -2392, -2352.
  • How fast a train makes its round trip. One Freight Car holds an hour of Plastic, so it hardly matters.
  • Power: the ceilings are sums of what the wiki says each machine draws. What the base really draws at each stage is not known until it runs.
  • Anything else the mods place in the world.
